author: Kristen Butler
title: Car Driving Erratically At High Speed Stopped By Grappler Technology - NewsBreak
text:
By Kristen Butler ,
14 hours ago Douglas County Sheriff's Office Like a real-life Batmobile, a Colorado State Patrol vehicle equipped with a Grappler stopped an out-of-control vehicle on Friday.
At around 9:35 a.m. Friday, 911 callers reported a vehicle driving erratically and hitting the median barrier at speeds of 75 mph on southbound Interstate 5 near Castle Pines, the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office said. A deputy spotted the driver and attempted to make a stop, but they kept going.
The deputy followed, working to block other traffic from the area of the erratic vehicle. A dashboard camera video shared by the sheriff’s office on Tuesday shows the runaway vehicle side-swiping the median and weaving in and out of marked lanes at high speed.
The deputy called for a vehicle equipped with Grappler technology, but the sheriff’s Grappler vehicles were not near enough to engage. Instead, deputies called for assistance from the Colorado State Patrol, which also has vehicles equipped with Grappler bumpers
The Grappler bumper deploys grapple lines that hook onto fleeing vehicles’ rear wheels, quickly stopping them without the need for more dangerous PIT maneuvers, which involve using a patrol vehicle to bump or tap the fleeing vehicle, often causing them to spin out.
The video shows a Colorado State Patrol truck deploy its Grappler, and the runaway vehicle is stopped within seconds. The sheriff’s office said the driver was taken into custody, but did not specify the nature of the charges, or a possible reason for the reckless driving.
“We appreciate the partnership with the Colorado State Patrol, and this goes to show the usefulness of this technology,” said Sheriff Darren Weekly. “Its also a reminder, if you drive recklessly or try to run from us, we will pursue you and we will catch you.”
